Response: Mongolia has established and is implementing partnerships that foster joint technology development and joint scientific research programmes for the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity, and that strengthen national scientific research and monitoring capabilities. These partnerships are enabled through national laws and policies supporting science, innovation and technology transfer, and are implemented through a mix of South–South, North–South and triangular/multilateral cooperation mechanisms. Mongolia participates in joint international research projects and programmes with multiple partner countries and institutions, and contributes to—and benefits from—global biodiversity data infrastructure and capacity-building initiatives to improve biodiversity information management, monitoring and evidence-based decision-making.

These partnerships are enabled through national laws and policies supporting science, innovation and technology transfer, and are implemented through a mix of South–South, North–South and triangular/multilateral cooperation mechanisms.
